keyChanges.title: Senior AI hardware director leaves Tesla for ex-Dojo startup DensityAI
keyChanges.description: Shishuang Sun, Tesla's Senior Director of AI Hardware Design, now lists DensityAI as his employer starting July 2026, in packaging and system hardware. The departure became public the week of Aug. 24. Sun spent more than five years on Tesla Dojo and Autopilot computers (principal engineer from Jan. 2021, promoted to senior director in April 2025) covering IC packaging, vertical power, signal/power integrity, PCB, and thermal/mechanical integration — the work that turns a tape-out into a board that ships. DensityAI was founded by former Dojo chief Ganesh Venkataramanan after Tesla wound down Dojo in 2025, and previously absorbed roughly 20 Tesla supercomputer engineers. Digitimes, Electrek, and Barchart/inkl all reported the move. Tesla has not disclosed a replacement. This is packaging talent leaving after AI5 tape-out and while AI6/Dojo 3 remain unproven, not a junior attrition story.

One executive exit does not by itself halt a foundry tape-out already submitted

Specialty is advanced packaging, power delivery, and thermals — the bottleneck after transistor design

Tesla still has no disclosed AI5 sample yield, board count, or volume date earlier than mid-2027

keyChanges.title: Musk claims AI5 is 2–3x Nvidia at 10% cost, while admitting the chip program 'wasn't closing'
keyChanges.description: A Ron Baron conversation clip circulated Aug. 24–27 in which Elon Musk said Tesla 'hinges' on AI5 for next-gen self-driving cars and Optimus, claimed inference performance per watt 'probably' 2–3x Nvidia at about 10% of Nvidia's chip cost, and said he has 'the entire physical design of the chip laid out in memory.' In the same remarks he said the AI5 program 'was in bad shape. It wasn't closing… and it really wasn't on a path to success,' that Dojo was 'not on a path to be competitive with NVIDIA,' and that he collapsed the two into one inference-chip program while Tesla 'continue[s] to use NVIDIA for training.' Wccftech (Aug. 25) and Digitimes (Aug. 27) carried the quotes. No new silicon, sample boards, or measured perf/watt numbers were released. Tesla also had no paper at Hot Chips 2026 (Aug. 23–25), where OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Waymo presented custom AI silicon. Tape-out was April 2026; volume is still mid-2027. Unverified 10x-cost claims do not change the sample/volume gap.

positive_signals: Musk restated that AI5 is taped out and is the single focused inference program after merging Dojo into it
He described AI5 as the chip for next-gen vehicles and Optimus, i.e. a committed product path rather than a cancelled Dojo-only effort
negative_signals: Musk admitted the AI5 program 'wasn't closing' and 'wasn't on a path to success' before he collapsed Dojo into it

No AI5 sample, yield, or board-count disclosure accompanied the clip
Tesla presented nothing at Hot Chips 2026 while peers disclosed custom inference silicon
Volume production remains a 2027 event, ~2 years after original HW5/AI5 timing

keyChanges.title: Samsung still 'improving SF2 yield' as TSMC already runs 2nm at 73% foundry share
keyChanges.description: Counterpoint's Q2 2026 pure-play foundry update (posted Aug. 26; Korea JoongAng Daily and Semiecosystem on Aug. 28) shows TSMC at 73% share for a second straight quarter, driven by 2nm mass production, 3nm ramp, and tight advanced packaging. Samsung Foundry is stuck at 7% share for four consecutive quarters (Q3 2025–Q2 2026), down from 9% in Q1 2025. Counterpoint's explicit note: Samsung's 'major target is still on improving SF2's yield rate,' with SF4/SF5 demand and H1 wafer price hikes carrying revenue — not a 2nm production win. Tesla's AI5/AI6 path depends on Samsung 2nm (including Taylor as the planned U.S. volume site). TSMC is already shipping 2nm commercially; Samsung is still in yield recovery. No Tesla wafer, yield, or Taylor trial-production confirmation was attached to this print. That is a foundry-partner lag, not a Tesla tape-out milestone.

That is a real ops feature, not a service launch. Tesla Oracle notes Tesla staff were in the passenger seats and that some of the units still had steering wheels — at odds with the wheel-free production Cybercab Tesla has been advertising. Teslarati also flags that color-only ID fails for blind and color-blind riders Tesla has courted. Teslarati’s claim that paid public Cybercab rides start Sept 3 overstates the invite-only Austin event; paid public Cybercab service remains at zero. Employee/staff Cybercab rides have been running for weeks.

keyChanges.title: Robotaxi claims 6am–10pm hours and a bigger unsupervised fleet — no count given
keyChanges.description: On Aug 26 the official @robotaxi account said Robotaxi now runs 6am–10pm, 7 days/week, that the unsupervised fleet is “a lot bigger,” and that “upgraded intelligence in vehicle distribution & routing” should cut wait times. Teslarati correctly notes this is a dispatch/logistics change, not a new FSD version. Tesla published no vehicle count, no city-by-city split, and no wait-time data. Austin previously advertised hours as late as 2am; Teslarati says the post does not say whether Austin kept that overnight window or was folded into a 10pm nationwide cutoff — a possible hours cut in the flagship city. Last verified unsupervised active fleet was still on the order of ~21 (July 23). Inventory stacking in Dallas and a Sept 3 Cybercab event do not change that paid Cybercab service is still unconfirmed and Model Y robotaxi utilization remains the constraint.

keyChanges.title: Brandenburg talks rural Tesla robotaxis — Tesla unconfirmed, German FSD still blocked
keyChanges.description: Brandenburg transport minister Robert Crumbach told Märkische Allgemeine the German state is in talks with companies “such as Tesla” about driverless shuttles for villages where buses run twice a day or not at all, folded into the existing Rufbus on-demand network. Tesla North reported the comments on Aug 25. Tesla has not confirmed a Brandenburg contract or Cybercab/Robotaxi deployment. A statewide rural rollout would still need legal approvals Crumbach himself said are not in place.

keyChanges.title: China still missing from Tesla FSD subscription list despite pullout denial
keyChanges.description: Tesla China denied Aug. 26 rumors that its Shanghai FSD data center had been vacated, telling Tencent Tech and National Business Daily the facility is operating normally, driver-assistance hiring is accelerating, and it reported the claims to police. The denial does not change the regulatory reality: Tesla's current 12-market FSD (Supervised) subscription list covers the US, Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, and the five EU consumer markets (Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium). China is not on that list. Tesla's US site still names China among markets where FSD Supervised is 'available for use,' a contradiction that has persisted since Tesla's May 2026 availability claim and the subsequent rename to 'Tesla Assisted Driving' on the China site with full features promised 'later.' Tesla has not published China subscription pricing or a broad Supervised rollout timeline. Consumer FSD markets tracked here remain at 6 (US + five EU countries). Korea stays a partial origin-split market; China is not a seventh national approval.

keyChanges.title: Swiss FSD ride-alongs continue; Tesla still has not filed with Astra
keyChanges.description: Tesla Europe posted 'FSD Supervised in Switzerland' on Aug. 23, amplifying passenger ride-alongs after Blick road-tested the system from Tesla's Zurich store to Adliswil. A Tesla employee activated FSD (Supervised); the car handled city and highway tasks with one aborted turn that required a human handoff. Tesla is offering supervised passenger demos at five Swiss locations and quoting about CHF 95/month, but Swiss owners still cannot subscribe. As of Blick's Aug. 20 report, Tesla had not filed a request with the Federal Roads Office (Astra). Switzerland remains outside Tesla's five approved EU consumer markets (Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Lithuania). Ride-alongs have existed since late 2025; this week's official amplification is marketing, not a regulatory filing or approval. Germany, France, Italy, and the UK also remain outside customer FSD.

keyChanges.title: XPeng funds IRON for end-2026 mass production while Tesla Optimus is still pre-revenue
keyChanges.description: On August 24 XPeng announced a >$900 million robotics round at a >$6.3 billion post-money valuation — billed as China's largest single-round private embodied-AI financing — led by IDG Capital with Gaorong, Tencent, and Alibaba. Official use of proceeds includes mass-production facilities. XPeng said next-gen IRON should enter mass production by the end of 2026, start inside XPeng stores and campuses, then launch with China and overseas deliveries in 2027. Electrek explicitly framed that schedule as staying ahead of Tesla's stalling Optimus program. XPeng's own Q2 print was weak (wider loss, missed revenue, stock down), and IRON's on-device autonomy claim is still a stage promise, not customer proof. Even so, a funded 2026 mass-production target from a scaled EV maker is a harder commercial clock than Tesla's elapsed August SOP window and H2 2027 'as early as' external sales.

keyChanges.title: Europe Q3 QTD cratering while EV market booms — Model Y 5,138 in July after 32,685 in June
keyChanges.description: No official Tesla Q3 2026 production/delivery print (still expected early October; street ~461.5k vs Q2 480k). Mid-quarter European registrations are the actual volume signal this week, and they are ugly. Dataforce via TeslaNorth and L'Automobile Magazine: Model Y topped Europe in June with 32,685 cars, then collapsed to 5,138 registrations and 73rd place in July — a typical Tesla end-of-quarter bunching pattern, but the trough is deeper than usual. BaseNor, citing Electrek's Fred Lambert, says Tesla Europe quarter-to-date through late August is the lowest comparable period on record; Norway printed 24 Tesla registrations in July (−97.1% YoY) and Spain 131 (−81.3% YoY). That is happening while Europe's overall BEV market is exploding: InsideEVs/Dataforce show July EV sales +51% YoY to 277,006 units (25% share), with Skoda Elroq, VW ID.4, and Renault 5 leading the month — none of Tesla's models. YTD optics still look fine: Model Y remains Europe's #1 EV through July at ~115,957 units (+55% YoY) and Focus2Move ranks it the world's best-selling car through seven months (+19.6%). Those rankings are backward-looking. They do not refill a Q3 hole that now requires an unusually large September dump, including Shanghai-to-Europe boats Lambert says are still in transit. Auto profit quality is unchanged: 1.4% operating margin, −$1.09B FCF, FY CapEx >$25B. A European miss on top of that would confirm the QoQ delivery step-down Street already models.

keyChanges.title: Cybertruck AWD/Premium hiked $5,000 with no spec change — volume product still not selling
keyChanges.description: Tesla quietly raised Dual Motor AWD from $69,990 to $74,990 and Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990 on the night of August 24; Cyberbeast stayed at $99,990. No range, towing, or hardware change. Teslarati framed the hike as demand returning. Reality is the opposite of a volume story: the same Dual Motor was dangled at $59,990 for ~10 days earlier this year, so the entry truck has swung $15,000 in months. InsideEVs cites an estimated 7,263 Cybertruck sales in H1 2026, down ~32% YoY, against a line Tesla built for ~250,000/year — roughly 94% below planned capacity. SpaceX/Musk entities were already inflating late-2025 registrations. Raising price on a stalled niche truck is margin extraction, not a demand recovery, and it does nothing for the Q3 delivery print. Teslarati's own review concedes the $60k AWD was the steal and $75k is a harder sell.

Nine years after the 2017 unveil, Semi is still a rounding error next to auto volume.

The strategy is U.S.-focused and tied to Einride's Saga AI platform (including Amazon work). Even if Tesla hits 75 this year, that is days of Model Y output, not a Class 8 ramp. 500 trucks through 2027 against a 50,000/year design plant is ~1% of nameplate. Tesla has not confirmed it can actually deliver 75 Semis in the next four months, and the public Semi configurator remains closed. Customer optimism is not a production print.

keyChanges.title: JETI school districts raise taxes as Terafab remains dirt work; first tax-roll hit 2029-30
keyChanges.description: Both Grimes County JETI districts adopted 2026-27 budgets Aug 27 and are raising tax rates now because Terafab has delivered almost no taxable value. Anderson-Shiro CISD approved a smaller $13.83 million budget but lifted its total rate ~13% to $1.0476 per $100; a trustee said 'Terafab has only done a little bit of dirt work,' and the district has received nothing beyond SpaceX's JETI application fees. Superintendent Sarah Borowitz told the board the first Terafab phase will not be fully on the tax rolls until the 2029-2030 school year — after a 10-year school-tax reduction per phase under the July 14 JETI deal. Iola ISD set a $0.9841 total rate (M&O $0.6341 + I&S $0.3500), about $130 more per $100,000 home, after pushing a bond payment later to stay under $1.00; the board is already banking on speculative Terafab value ('under $100 million' next year, '$1 billion' the year after) even while saying finances survive if the project stalls. Headline JETI relief is years away; local taxpayers are paying more in the meantime.
